You're auditing PR #75 in the zimmermann-pwa repo (ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa), authored by Tim Lavelle (project tech lead). This is a tiny, tightly-scoped CI-config-only PR: `fix/release-v0.1.0-sit-gate-recovery` → base `release/v0.1.0`. 2 files changed, +22/-1 lines total. No application code touched. Given the size, run 2 focused angles yourself rather than a big fan-out: (a) correctness/regression, (b) security/failure-modes. No styling/token or contract-fidelity angle applies here — skip those.

## Full diff

index 94950a2e..495ab371 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
@@ -33,8 +33,19 @@ jobs:
       - name: Install Playwright browsers
         run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium
 
+      # Provisional: no *.p0.spec files exist anywhere in the repo yet (still early

+      - name: Warn if no P0 specs exist yet
+        run: |
+          if ! find e2e/tests/zimm -name '*.p0.spec.*' | grep -q .; then
+            echo "::warning title=No P0 coverage::playwright-p0 passed with zero matching specs — this SIT gate is not verifying any P0 journey yet. See .claude/skills/qa-generate."

       - name: Run P0 suite

## Full head-state lighthouserc.js (for context — only the `settings` block above is new)

```js
module.exports = {
  ci: {
    collect: {
      url: [process.env.LHCI_TARGET_URL || 'http://localhost:3000'],
      numberOfRuns: 3,
      settings: {
        extraHeaders: process.env.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL
          ? {'x-sfdc-access-control': process.env.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL}
          : undefined,
      },
    },
    assert: {
      preset: 'lighthouse:recommended',
      assertions: {
        'categories:performance': ['error', { minScore: 0.8 }],
        'categories:accessibility': ['error', { minScore: 0.9 }],
        'categories:best-practices': ['error', { minScore: 0.9 }],
        // Trend gate: block if score drops > 5 pts vs stored baseline.
        // Requires LHCI server — set LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL + LHCI_TOKEN in GitHub secrets.
      },
    },
    upload: {
      target: process.env.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL ? 'lhci' : 'temporary-public-storage',
      serverBaseUrl: process.env.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL,
      token: process.env.LHCI_TOKEN,
    },
  },
};
```

## Ground truth I've already established myself (don't re-fetch CI logs — I have the authoritative numbers; spend your budget reading repo source instead)

- No Jira ticket is referenced anywhere (branch name, PR body, commit message) — this is ticket-less release/CI engineering, confirmed not an oversight to chase further.
- Baseline (pre-PR, 2026-08-05 run on release/v0.1.0): `playwright-p0` hard-failed "No tests found"; `lighthouse-ci` failed with `CHROME_INTERSTITIAL_ERROR` hitting `http://localhost:3000` (because `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` secret was unset, so `LHCI_TARGET_URL` env resolved empty and the `|| 'http://localhost:3000'` fallback kicked in against nothing listening). Confirmed via actual job logs — Tim's PR description accurately diagnoses this.
- On this PR's own head run: `playwright-p0` now SUCCEEDS via soft-pass, and the `::warning title=No P0 coverage::...` annotation fired exactly as designed (confirmed in the actual job log). This part works correctly, verified.
- `lighthouse-ci` on this PR's head run no longer hits CHROME_INTERSTITIAL_ERROR — it successfully reaches the real SIT MRT URL (confirmed: "Uploading median LHR of ***...success!" — it collected 3 real runs and uploaded to the LHCI server). So the URL/header fix works mechanically. BUT the job still fails (exit 1) because of 12 real `error`-level assertion failures against actual (bad) site performance: `categories.performance` found 0.41 vs expected ≥0.8, `categories.best-practices` found 0.83 vs expected ≥0.9, plus `csp-xss`, `errors-in-console`, `inspector-issues`, `installable-manifest`, `maskable-icon`, `service-worker`, `splash-screen`, `unused-javascript`, `uses-rel-preconnect`, `valid-source-maps` all at 0/failing (all part of the pre-existing, untouched `lighthouse:recommended` preset — Tim's diff did not change `assert.preset` or the assertions block at all). `categories.accessibility` passed. This is a genuine, pre-existing site-quality gap on whatever `develop` build Tim manually deployed to SIT (via `npm run push:sit`, mentioned in the PR body as a manual action, not part of the diff) — NOT something introduced by or fixable within this 2-file diff. I'm treating this as correctly out of scope for this PR — do not report it as a defect in the diff itself. I already plan to flag it separately as a discovery, not as an in-scope finding.
- "Publish Playwright report to Pages" job (a separate job in the same workflow, NOT touched by this diff, NOT part of the `sit-gate` job's `needs:` list) fails identically on both the baseline run and this PR's run — empty `steps` array both times, meaning it fails during job setup (consistent with a GitHub Pages/environment config issue). Confirmed pre-existing baseline debt via direct comparison of both runs' job lists — not in scope, don't re-flag it as new.
- Both changed files (`lighthouserc.js`, `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml`) are Tier 1 per `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and correctly routed to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` in `CODEOWNERS` (lines for `lighthouserc.js` and `.github/workflows/`). The repo's `tier1-guard` check fired correctly and listed both files. This part of the process is working correctly — don't re-verify unless you spot something I'd have missed (e.g. a glob gap in CODEOWNERS that doesn't actually match one of these two exact paths — worth a quick double check).
- `node -c lighthouserc.js` passes (valid JS syntax) at head.

## What I need from you

**(a) Correctness/regression:**
1. Read `playwright.config.*` (read-only — it's Tier 1 test config, don't propose editing it) and confirm the `p0` project's test-matching pattern actually aligns with the `find e2e/tests/zimm -name '*.p0.spec.*'` glob this PR's new warning step uses. I want to know if the glob is a faithful proxy for "playwright will actually match zero p0 tests," or if it could drift out of sync (e.g., if the p0 project's `testMatch` is scoped differently than a flat `*.p0.spec.*` search under `e2e/tests/zimm`). Check `.claude/rules/testing.md`'s documented naming convention too (`SFCC-NNN_description.p0.spec.ts`) for corroboration.
2. Is `--pass-with-no-tests` a real, documented Playwright Test CLI flag? Confirm via `node_modules/@playwright/test` or `node_modules/playwright/` docs/source if present, or via package.json's playwright version and known CLI flags for that version.
3. Any bug in the bash conditional (`if ! find ... | grep -q .; then ... fi`) — edge cases, quoting, exit-code handling.
4. Does `extraHeaders: ... : undefined` behave correctly when `LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` is unset (i.e., does passing `extraHeaders: undefined` to lighthouse-ci's `collect.settings` behave the same as omitting the key entirely, or could it throw / behave unexpectedly)? Check `node_modules/@lhci/cli` or `node_modules/lighthouse` if helpful, or reason from how the config is consumed.
5. Check other workflows (`deploy-test.yml`, `deploy-sit.yml` if it exists, any other `.github/workflows/*.yml` referencing `LHCI_TARGET_URL` or Lighthouse) for naming consistency — does this PR's approach (secret `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` mapped to generic env var `LHCI_TARGET_URL`) match a pattern used elsewhere, or could it collide/confuse across tiers?

**(b) Security/failure-modes:**
1. Could the real value of `LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` leak into any artifact with broader read access than "GitHub Actions secrets + the SIT environment itself"? Specifically: does a standard `lhci autorun` LHR JSON (what gets written to `.lighthouseci/` and/or uploaded to an LHCI server) ever include raw request headers sent during the Lighthouse run? I believe standard LHR JSON's `audits['network-requests']` does NOT include request headers (only url/timing/size/status fields) — verify this against the actual installed `lighthouse`/`@lhci/cli` package in `node_modules` if you can find schema/source evidence, and tell me if my belief is right, wrong, or unconfirmable from what's available in this repo. Note GitHub's own log redaction already confirmed masking the literal secret value in log text (`LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL: ***`), so the concern is specifically about the LHR JSON artifact/LHCI-server-stored content, not the Action log.
2. Any other secret-handling issue in the diff (e.g., a secret echoed in a way that wouldn't be auto-masked, a secret passed on a command line where it'd show in `ps`, etc.)?
3. Does the new header get sent anywhere it shouldn't (e.g., to the `http://localhost:3000` fallback path when running against a non-SIT target)? Confirm the ternary correctly scopes it to only when `LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` is actually set.

Report findings in the standard format (file:line, summary, failure scenario, category). Be precise about CONFIRMED vs something you couldn't fully verify — say what would settle it if you can't. Keep the report tight; this is a small diff, I don't need padding.

name: SIT Gate

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  playwright-p0:
    name: Playwright P0 journeys
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-playwright-report:
    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

# PR #75 Audit — `fix/release-v0.1.0-sit-gate-recovery` → `release/v0.1.0`

Verified the pasted diff against the real refs first: `git diff origin/release/v0.1.0...origin/fix/release-v0.1.0-sit-gate-recovery` reproduces it byte-for-byte (file counts +14/-1 and +8/-0 match your "+22/-1" total). All findings below trace to the real branches, not my local working tree (which is on an unrelated feature branch).

---

## (a) Correctness / regression

**A1. 🟡 should-fix — CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml:41-45` vs `playwright.config.js:54`.
The new `find e2e/tests/zimm -name '*.p0.spec.*'` check is **not** a faithful proxy for "Playwright will match zero p0 tests" — it's narrower than the `p0` project's real resolution. `playwright.config.js:14` sets `testDir: './e2e'`; the `p0` project (line 54) sets `testMatch: ['**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}']` with no further directory restriction, so it matches anywhere under the whole `e2e/` tree, not just `e2e/tests/zimm`.

I proved this rather than just reasoning about it: created `e2e/fixtures/__probe__/stray-outside-zimm.p0.spec.ts` (a real, valid spec, outside the conventional directory), ran both checks, then deleted it (`git status --short` clean before and after):
```
=== Playwright p0 project's view (--list) ===
[p0] › fixtures/__probe__/stray-outside-zimm.p0.spec.ts:2:5 › stray p0 spec outside e2e/tests/zimm
Total: 1 test in 1 file
=== Bash proxy's view ===
NOT FOUND (warning WOULD fire)
```
A real p0 spec placed outside `e2e/tests/zimm/` would actually run under Playwright, but the new step would still emit `::warning title=No P0 coverage::...` — a false "zero coverage" claim despite real coverage executing. This doesn't affect gate pass/fail (that's driven by the real Playwright run), only the warning's own accuracy — which is its entire purpose. Currently dormant only because every spec in the repo today genuinely lives under `e2e/tests/zimm/` (confirmed: `find e2e -iname '*.spec.*'` returns only files under that tree). Secondary, unexecuted (PLAUSIBLE) mirror case: the bash glob's trailing `*` also matches extensions Playwright's `{js,ts}` restriction wouldn't (e.g. a typo'd `.p0.spec.jsx`), which would suppress the warning while contributing zero real coverage — same root cause, opposite direction.

**A2. Clean — CONFIRMED by execution.** `--pass-with-no-tests` is real. `--help` on the installed binary (version confirmed `1.60.0` via `playwright --version`, matching `package.json`'s `^1.60.0` and the resolved version in `package-lock.json` on **both** `release/v0.1.0` and the PR head branch) shows: `--pass-with-no-tests  Makes test run succeed even if no tests were [found]`. Ran the exact CI command against the repo's real current state (zero `*.p0.spec.*` files exist anywhere):
```
$ playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github                    → "Error: No tests found", exit 1
$ playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github --pass-with-no-tests → exit 0, playwright-report/index.html still generated
```
Matches the documented baseline and the fix exactly. The html reporter producing a valid report even at zero tests also means the later "Upload Playwright report" artifact step won't fail on a missing directory.

**A3. Clean — CONFIRMED.** Bash conditional has no bug. Ran it verbatim (fires correctly today). Also simulated GitHub Actions' real default `run:` shell for Linux (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}` — pipefail is **on** by default) against a nonexistent-directory edge case: `find`'s stderr doesn't abort the step, because the failing pipeline is the direct test-condition of `if !`, which bash exempts from `errexit`. No quoting issues; the script has no `exit` of its own so it always returns 0 regardless of branch taken, matching its "warn, never gate" intent.

**A4. Clean — CONFIRMED via source.** `extraHeaders: ... : undefined` is handled correctly when unset. Traced to the actual consumption site: `node_modules/lighthouse/lighthouse-core/gather/driver/prepare.js:114-115` — `const headers = settings.extraHeaders; if (headers) await session.sendCommand(...)`. A plain truthy check; `undefined` and lighthouse's own default (`null`, `config/constants.js:117`) both correctly skip attaching any header. No crash path in the config-merge chain.

**A5. Clean, angle now vacuous.** Grepped every file in `.github/workflows/` for `LHCI_TARGET_URL|LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL|lighthouserc|lhci`: only `digital-sit.yml` matches (plus `protected-file-guard.yml`'s two unrelated path globs). No other workflow touches Lighthouse at all, so there's no established pattern to collide with or diverge from.
